chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I have inherited wealth, and I know that its owner, from whom I inherited it, used to deal in usury. I know that there is usury in it, and I am certain of this, but its permissibility does not feel right to me due to my knowledge of it. I asked the jurists of Iraq and the Hijaz, and they said: 'It is not permissible for you to consume it because of what is in it.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him:

'If you know that a specific amount in it is usury, and you know its owners, then take your principal capital and return the rest. If it is mixed, then consume it entirely, for the wealth is yours. Avoid what the owner used to do. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) abolished the usury that had passed and forbade what remained. Whoever was ignorant of it, his ignorance was excused until he knew it. When he knew its prohibition, it became forbidden for him, and punishment became obligatory upon him if he incurred it, just as it is obligatory upon whoever eats usury.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on inherited wealth that contains usury (riba)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on inherited wealth containing usury, distinguishing between identifiable and mixed riba. He notes that while past usury is abolished, remaining usury is forbidden, and ignorance serves as an excuse until one gains knowledge, after which the prohibition and accountability apply.
